This script is meant for testing OTU table given pet ownership status. Test results will be further checked via enrichment analysis in separate script.

```{r}
library(phyloseq)
library(tidyverse)
meta <- read.table("/N/project/Watson_AGP/Zhengxu/DataSet/cleaned/meta/meta_07202026.txt")
load("/N/u/liaozh/Quartz/Desktop/Link to Zhengxu/DataSet/cleaned/biom/biom_07202026.Rdata")
```

Try ANCOM-BC for analysis.

```{r}
# if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly=TRUE))
#     install.packages("BiocManager")
# BiocManager::install("ANCOMBC")
library(ANCOMBC)
```

The following code has been revised on 07302025, removed those three samples. Now we have 4166 samples.


```{r}
rownames(meta) <- meta$ID

meta_data <- meta%>%
  select(pet_status, age,
         sleep_duration_regroup,
         sex ,
         race_recode ,smoker, exercise_recode ,
         alcohol_recode ,
         education_recode ,
         bmi,
         protein_intake ,
         antibiotic_recent_take)
biom@otu_table <- otu_table(subset(biom@otu_table,select = meta$ID))
test <- phyloseq(otu_table(biom@otu_table,taxa_are_rows = T),sample_data(data.frame(meta_data)))

out <- ancombc2(data = test,
              fix_formula = "pet_status + age + sleep_duration_regroup + sex + race_recode + smoker + exercise_recode + alcohol_recode + education_recode + bmi + protein_intake + antibiotic_recent_take", 
              rand_formula = NULL,  # random formula is for sample-specific random effect
              p_adj_method = "hochberg", # Benjamini-Hochberg
              prv_cut = 0.10, # Taxa less than prv_cut will be removed
              lib_cut = 0,  # lib_cut=0 means no sample will be removed from analysis
              group = "pet_status", # primary interest variable
              struc_zero = TRUE,  # detect structural zeros based on group
              neg_lb = FALSE,  # not classify a taxon as a structural zero using its asymptotic lower bound (proportion test)
              em_control = list(tol = 1e-5, max_iter = 100),  # set tolerance of gap, and maximum iteration times
              alpha = 0.05, 
              global = TRUE, # global test
              pairwise = TRUE, # pairwise directional test, do we need to? Try it and just check
              n_cl = 1, # paralleled computing
              verbose = FALSE) # show warnings, could be set as FALSE

res_prim = out$res
res_global = out$res_global
res_pair = out$res_pair
```


Note: This package applies a sensitivity analysis over *psudo-counts* for 0 in log-transformation.
This analysis involves adding a series of pseudo-counts (ranging from 0.01 to 0.5 in increments of 0.01) to the zero counts of each taxon.

```{r}
results_less_alpha <- res_global[res_global$q_val<0.05,]
# 176 taxa
results_both_pass <- results_less_alpha[results_less_alpha$passed_ss,]
# 82 taxa
```

Give out the taxa info of each found taxa (just combine the found taxa and their detailed info from biom data)

```{r}
taxa_results_less_alpha <- biom@tax_table[results_less_alpha$taxon,]
taxa_results_both_pass <- biom@tax_table[results_both_pass$taxon,]
```


```{r}
write.csv(res_global, '~/Desktop/Link to Zhengxu/Analysis/Results/res_global.csv')
write.csv(res_pair, '~/Desktop/Link to Zhengxu/Analysis/Results/res_pair.csv')
taxa_info <- as.data.frame(biom@tax_table[res_global$taxon,])
taxa_info$taxa <- rownames(taxa_info)
write.csv(taxa_info,'~/Desktop/Link to Zhengxu/Analysis/Results/taxa_name.csv')
```
